title: RTS made 100% by AI. 2.2 billion tokens. How it was done, described in 4033 characters long post
author: Famous_Ad_5611
selftext:
Operation Husaria is a RTS in the style of the good old 90s classics - so we get Poland vs Great Owner of Green Units. And it has hussars, amber harvesting, two campaigns and FMV briefings (partial ;p).

Game: [https://maxdemage.itch.io/operation-husaria-rts](https://maxdemage.itch.io/operation-husaria-rts)

It's fully AI-made (hence the title). I wrote about 40 words, the tokens went brrrrrrrrt bop bap brrrrrrt, and a game came out.

Here's the whole **workflow**:

1. It started with a brief of 30–40 words. Roughly: "90s-style RTS, Poland vs Russia, basic units with upgrades, make it 3D so probably install Blender, playable in browser." Maybe a few more words than that.
2. Setup was WSL on Windows, plus T3 Code as the orchestrator. That's about it. The whole "setup phase" was me thinking "hey, let's install an orchestrator."
3. Opus 5.5 as the lead, Opus 5.5 as the workers. No Sonnet, no Fable. Pure Opus all the way down.
4. The first AI run just expanded the brief. No skills and no plan (!). I didn't want a step-by-step guide, just a better spec of what the game is. My 40 words came back as \~24,000 words of design docs: factions, buildings, tech trees, 60 units with stats and voice lines, and two 14-mission campaigns.
5. I read it and changed almost nothing (censored some memes, made few memes stronger)
6. Then came the big step. I opened the project in T3 and asked it, and I quote: "build game from brief".
7. And it just... did. Under the hood T3 orchestrates everything: code, builds, tests, playtests and golden replay runs (the sim is deterministic, so a replay hash catches any change in behaviour). It checks its own screenshots, adds music, and writes the missions and their scripts. Every 3D model is a blender python script it wrote.
8. The tokens run out in a 5h session, so T3 snoozes, waits for the reset and starts working again. And again, and again... and... again.
9. The first playable version came after 5 sessions. Honestly, amazing that it worked. It had 6 missions and the core game. Another round of only missions and missing units and ... it was done.
10. But the UI was shit. Obviously, duh. AI! I brainstormed with Gemini and we landed on: what if the HUD is a TV news station? I googled a few news broadcast screenshots, dropped them into T3 and asked it to do its magic (and to always show me screenshots of its work). Now your objectives scroll in the news crawl, and the minimap is a weather map xD
11. Polish is where a bit of human input came in. I played, wrote down what felt off and pushed the notes to T3. Then I repeated that. The orchestrator is an amazing tool. It took me about 4h of gameplay.
12. I wanted proper 90s full-motion video cutscenes but the opus scripts were weak, so this is the part I wrote myself. After manual script I used gemini hydrogen to write image prompts, then nano banana image generation for the character sheets and gemini's video generation for the shots. I cut the story into 10-second bits and went step by step. I threw the clips at T3 and asked it to combine them. It now plays them with VHS tracking glitches on a wall of old TVs. No idea how.
13. Every unit needs its "Yes, commander?" lines like in good old days so T3 wrote a script that gives every unit a voice and generates the lines through Elevenlabs. The free tier was enough for all 600 of them. Production value: yup, still $0. (The voice lines are only polish.. this is where I don't have enough credits xD)
14. I asked for an itch build with all the graphics, covers, background, and got one.

Now the fun part - the bill: accroding to T3 its 2.2 billion tokens. 

That's around $800 at API prices also acording to T3. 

Buuuuut - I'm on a normal $100 subscription (plus the ElevenLabs free tier), and I still had a reset left after end of all this ;D

  
Some numbers from the repo:

* 40-word brief → 24k words of design docs
* 60k lines of type script, 17k lines of blender python
* 92 scripted 3D models, 60 units (30 per side), 28 missions
* 100 test files, including browser tests that take screenshots
* 590 voice lines (ElevenLabs, free tier)

  
So?

Is it a good game? I had fun playing it, so I'd say good *enough*. For $100 of production value...



Game dev is apparently doomed.

comments.author: doc4geo
comments.body: Game is good if the mechanics is good. AI haters will change their mind soon

comments.author: AdminClown
comments.body:
This is a prototype not a game. 

>I wrote about 40 words, the tokens went brrrrrrrrt bop bap brrrrrrt, and a game came out.

This is not a flex.

replies.author: Famous_Ad_5611
replies.body:
Now - I know where this comes from. I dabbled in game dev since like 20 years xD - It should be like you say: a prototype. But is it an actual prototype if it has so much content? It's not only one level. It's not only 5 units. It's not just one mechanic. Or is it more like a poors man game? 

The whole "prototype" accusation, in 90% of cases is correct. But it feels like we should  use this "type of attack" a bit more carefully. ;)

replies.author: AdminClown
replies.body:
It looks absolutely horrible as a "finished game" and not a single person outside of you would spend more than 5 minutes on it.

You and your post are exactly the reason why the general public is so resistant to the idea of AI game development. 2.2 billion tokens on what you have posted is the definition of waste.

The lack of care shown by you and many others that engage in this "a few prompts, game complete" are the bane of the existence of any other dedicated dev in the AI dev scene. And dedicated and passionate devs will suffer with AI scrutiny because of you and others like you.

You even admit to it below:

>And i tought - hey listen what if i make ai slop.

Things like this should be an instant ban from this community and any like it.

replies.author: Famous_Ad_5611
replies.body:
Its funny how we argue not knowing about who we are and what is our situation. 

Sometimes people will do stupid things just for themselfs, this was one of those things. An experiment. Never wanted to show it off - just to build it, test it and see what it's there. I do those kind of things to understand how system works, how to connect to ceratain solutions, how easy is to use certain APIs and so on. So yes, the idea was - hey listen what if i make ai slop. And, that is not something bad to do, right? I wanted to experiment and try it. What is wrong with experimenting? What is wrong with trying to do some stupid things to learn something? What is wrong with me wasting my time and my moeny on my experiments? You'll propobly say that I should keep it to myself then... like I wrote, after seeing how things work, I wanted to actually show my workflow. Maybe someone will see something and benefit from it.

But on the other hand - now if I would take this game and put 200 hours into it, manually adjusting, tweaking and adding juice and polish,  what would that change? Would that 200 hours overshadow the fact that 80% of the game was "one prompted"? 

I spent - I think - thousands of hours on gamedev, and many many more on other dev activities - that is my work, and also my hobby since more than 20 years. 

Yet I will not ban anyone from trying to have fun. Instead I will encurage them to use better tools, to add more of thier time and care into project. 

But than again on the yet another 'other' hand - that stupid AI just one shot a (lets you your wording) a playable prototype in 2 days. Damn thats wicked.

replies.author: AdminClown
replies.body:
>But on the other hand - now if I would take this game and put 200 hours into it, manually adjusting, tweaking and adding juice and polish, what would that change? Would that 200 hours overshadow the fact that 80% of the game was "one prompted"?

No one is asking you to manually do things by hand. Your lack of care is just obvious and should be discouraged. There is nothing to learn from your post quite the contrary it serves as "what not to do".

>I spent - I think - thousands of hours on gamedev, and many many more on other dev activities - that is my work, and also my hobby since more than 20 years.

Highly doubtful.

replies.author: Famous_Ad_5611
replies.body:
Now, it seems you just want to argue for the sake of arguing... I'm not even mad - I'm genuinely curious why.

I get why you'd be doubtful about my experience. You're entitled to be. Duh! Internet! But why focus on that one part and completely ignore the fact that you're advocating banning people for experimenting and having fun, and maybe throwing in some wisdom from that experiment?

Now, if I wanted to be a prick, I'd ask: do you just want to ban people because you're trying to gatekeep your little hobby? ;p

replies.author: Xinnobun
replies.body: I spent 100 years as a game dev. Trust me bro

replies.author: Kosh_Ascadian
replies.body:
>Would that 200 hours overshadow the fact that 80% of the game was "one prompted"?

Hours wise its meaningless. You could spend 200 hours and change nothing. 

But if I take it on good faith that those 200 hours would be spent actually polishing, adding your own human taste and ideas to the game then it would greatly improve the game yes. I'm not sure why this is even a question?

comments.author: Xinnobun
comments.body: Am I the only one who doesn't care how many tokens it took to produce a game? I wouldn't bat an eye even if you said it took 800 quadrillion tokens.

replies.author: Kosh_Ascadian
replies.body:
I mean, I care.

But kind of in the opposite way. If someone says they spent millions of tokens oneshotting something without human input I am just greatly saddened at the waste of resources.

replies.author: Xinnobun
replies.body: It doesn't affect me. People waste resources on all sorts of things every day, I acknowledge it but I don't dwell on it. I'm interested in what people actually manage to create, not how many tokens they burned getting there.

comments.author: Kosh_Ascadian
comments.body:
What is/was the goal here? Both having AI make this project wise and this post wise?

I'm a gamedev from way back and I don't at all understand, but would like to understand.

Like why do people spend actual money and actual world resources on this?

For context: Using AI as a tool to help build your creative vision faster or at a higher scope I understand. There's no question from me on why that is done.

replies.author: Famous_Ad_5611
replies.body:
I think the goal was - a bit weird. I see here a lot of games that are completely ai slop like. And i tought - hey listen what if i make ai slop. What if for once I don't use 100's of hours of my time to fine tune a game but just you know, "prompt it". And it made not a completely bad game [it's not a masterpiece I know]... but I don't think it's a total shit. 

So - This was my journey and I think I wanted to show that it can be done and not produce a complete garbage. Maybe some "aigamedev" will see this and use those few simple things to make their game better.

And again no money spent (except for ai subscription). So almost no money spent :p

replies.author: cratercamper
replies.body: Played 3 missions and enjoyed it. Art is interesting, game is playable. What is your problem? As gamedev you don't understand that AI as a tool can help us immensely with building the whole thing and doing the slave work and leave us with much more time to work on gameplay?

replies.author: Kosh_Ascadian
replies.body:
Where did I express I have a problem?

Where did I express I do not understand AI as a tool? I literally said I understand its use as a tool.

Your example of AI gamedev benefits is also not really applicable as in this one OP did almost nothing. Its a fully AI game. Hence my question, its not tool use, its not leaving more time for the human. It leaves 0 time for the human because the human decided to do nothing.

replies.author: cratercamper
replies.body: So? It is nice showcase what AI can do then and what humans can start to build on. ...that is your goal you are asking about.

replies.author: Kosh_Ascadian
replies.body:
Well then answer that maybe?

Instead of randomly going off on me having a problem and telling me how great AI development is.

replies.author: cratercamper
replies.body: The goal of it and why someone would spend money on it is: It is nice showcase what AI can do and what humans can start to build on.

comments.author: Bananaskovitch
comments.body: This is not the flex you think it is. It's more a benchmark exercise to test models than anything else. Sorry, but these flex about how little you did prompt and how many tokens it ate is exactly why AI game dev is frowned upon right now. It's easy to have somewhat of a skeleton when starting. The real job is in the infinite iteration you do after and the testing you do yourself.

replies.author: Famous_Ad_5611
replies.body:
You might not belive but I absolutely agree.

This was a experiment not a flex. I wanted to do "ai slop one prompt game". But it came out not as bad... so I shared the workflow. Maybe someone who has passion to spend time to fine tune and iterate will use some advice in their workflow ( eleven labs for voice, or t3, or the specification instead of plan). So yeah. That was my idea ;)
